claims.claim: brew install altairalabs/tap/promptarena installs PromptArena (Homebrew tap altairalabs/tap)
go install github.com/AltairaLabs/promptarena/v2/arena/cmd/promptarena@latest builds the promptarena binary
Go install builds from source and needs a C compiler and audio dev headers
promptarena --version prints version information
promptarena --version output includes PromptArena version information
promptarena init [project-name] is a valid command
promptarena init has a --quick flag that uses defaults and skips interactive prompts
promptarena init has a --provider flag; openai is an accepted value
init creates a project directory named after the project-name argument (my-first-test) that the reader then cd's into
init creates a complete test project in seconds
init creates config.arena.yaml (arena configuration) in the project
init creates prompts/assistant.yaml
init creates providers/openai.yaml
init creates scenarios/basic-test.yaml
init creates a .env file for environment setup
mkdir -p prompts providers scenarios creates the directories used by the manual path
The manual path creates prompts/greeter.yaml
apiVersion value promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 is the accepted apiVersion for PromptConfig, Provider, Scenario and Arena kinds
kind: PromptConfig is a valid kind
metadata.name is a field of a PromptConfig resource
spec.task_type is a string field of PromptConfig
spec.system_template is a PromptConfig field holding the system instructions
metadata.name identifies the prompt config and is referenced by the arena config (id: greeter)
spec.task_type links a scenario to the prompt config with the matching task_type
kind: Provider is a valid kind
spec.type is a Provider field
spec.model is a Provider field
gpt-4o-mini is a model name the openai provider accepts
spec.defaults is a Provider field holding model parameters
spec.defaults.temperature is a float parameter and 0.7 is accepted
spec.defaults.max_tokens is an integer parameter and 150 is accepted
spec.type accepts the values openai, anthropic and gemini
OPENAI_API_KEY is read automatically by the openai provider with no config field
OPENAI_API_KEY is the environment variable name for the OpenAI API key
scenario spec.task_type links the scenario to prompts/greeter.yaml (task_type greeting)
metadata.labels is a Scenario field accepting key-value labels
label category: basic is accepted on a Scenario
kind: Scenario is a valid kind
spec.turns is a Scenario field holding an array of turns
role: user is a valid turn role and each user turn triggers an LLM response
turn content is a string field
a turn accepts an assertions list
content_includes is a registered assertion type
assertion params is a field on each assertion
content_includes accepts params.patterns as a list of strings
assertion params.message is an accepted field used as the failure message
content_matches is a registered assertion type
content_matches accepts params.pattern as a regular expression
params.message on content_matches is the failure message
apiVersion and kind are standard PromptKit resource identifiers for Scenario resources
kind: Arena is a valid kind for config.arena.yaml
spec.prompt_configs is an Arena field, a list of entries with id and file
prompt_configs entries accept an id field
prompt_configs entries accept a file field
spec.providers is an Arena field, a list of entries with a file field
spec.scenarios is an Arena field, a list of entries with a file field
config.arena.yaml tells Arena which configurations to load and how to connect them
promptarena run with no arguments uses config.arena.yaml in the current directory
promptarena run is a valid command
promptarena run prints 'PromptArena Starting...' before loading
run prints 'Loading configuration...' and per-kind counts ('Loaded 1 prompt config', 'Loaded 1 provider', 'Loaded 1 scenario')
run prints 'Running tests...' and one line per turn in the form 'Scenario Name - Turn N [provider-name] (time)'
the scenario is displayed as 'Basic Greeting' in run output
run prints a Results summary with Total turns, Passed, Failed and Pass Rate
run prints 'Reports generated' and lists out/results.json
default output directory is out
the JSON report is written to out/results.json
cat out/results.json shows the JSON results
promptarena run --format markdown is valid and produces a Markdown report
the Markdown report is written to out/results.md
Arena loads the prompt, provider and scenario files on run
For each turn Arena takes the system prompt from greeter.yaml
For each turn Arena fills in the user message template
Arena sends the complete prompt to OpenAI
Arena checks each response against the turn assertions
content_matches ensures the response matches the expected pattern
Arena saves results in multiple formats
an assertion block with type content_includes and content_matches is valid in a turn without a message on content_includes
promptarena run re-runs the edited scenario
labels.category: edge-case is accepted on a Scenario
a turn with role user and empty content is accepted by the schema and runner
content_matches pattern ^.{10,}$ matches responses of at least 10 characters
config.arena.yaml scenarios list accepts multiple entries
spec.defaults.temperature accepts 0.2
temperature 0.2 is more deterministic
Lower temperature gives more consistent responses
export PATH=$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin fixes 'command not found' for a go install
echo $OPENAI_API_KEY should output a value beginning with sk-
the error 'No scenarios found' is printed when config.arena.yaml scenario paths do not match the directory structure
the reader's prompts/, providers/ and scenarios/ directories are the paths the config references
a failed assertion prints the message in the output
the failure output shows the actual response
link /arena/tutorials/02-multi-provider/ targets Tutorial 2 (Multi-Provider Testing)
link /arena/tutorials/03-multi-turn/ targets Tutorial 3 (Multi-Turn Conversations)
link /arena/how-to/scenarios/write-scenarios/ targets How-To: Write Scenarios
gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini are valid model names for the openai provider
promptarena run --format markdown generates a Markdown report
Tutorial 2 tests the same scenario across OpenAI, Claude and Gemini providers
